analysis.title: Overhead Supply: Running Into Resistance as Macro Headwinds Intensify
key_insights: SPX has rallied about 4% in five days from 7350 lows a week ago but remains below last Thursday's highs, its recent downtrend line and the 50 DMA. BTIG sees the market as vulnerable to another rollover now that oversold conditions have been relieved.
BTIG expects SPX, NDX and SOX to be nearing the end of their recent bounces and to move lower into next week.
SPX downtrend line sits near 7700. A move above it would be a strong signal for bulls, but BTIG expects SPX to stall below it and turn lower.

SOXX has bounced sharply and is back at its 200 DMA and six months of overhead supply. It could fill its October gap near $169, with little upside seen beyond that. A close above $175 would make BTIG reconsider its cautious stance.
The Bloomberg Dollar Index (BBDXY) is breaking out of a multi-year range (described as an 18-month base in the summary).
2-year yields posted their biggest two-day gain in over two years after Tuesday's hotter than expected CPI report. Inflation swaps have not reacted the same way.
Bitcoin is down nearly 20% from recent highs and has lost its 200 DMA. BTIG sees downside risk to about 66k and treats Bitcoin as a tell for liquidity.
Gold made fresh lows. Strength in gold miners (GDX) had looked like a bullish tell, but BTIG says the path of least resistance for precious metals is lower, with $3500 still likely.
The bull case BTIG acknowledges is that the market has traded well given recent events and price action in Nvidia (NVDA, Not Rated). BTIG says other issues outweigh it.
